title: Sensation, perception and psychophysics
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn how the senses turn physical energy into experience, and how to measure it: psychophysical methods, thresholds and Weber's law, signal detection theory, psychometric functions, the eye and early vision, color, the visual cortex and receptive fields, object and face recognition, motion and depth, hearing and sound localization, touch, pain, taste and smell, and perception as inference, including Bayesian cue combination, with analyses in Python.
primary_reading: Neuroscience Online, an open-access textbook from McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston (free)

weeks.5: The eye, the retina and early vision
weeks.7: The visual cortex and receptive fields
weeks.12: Perception as inference: Bayesian cue combination

blocks.deliverable: Estimate a threshold from supplied staircase data.
Compute d-prime and criterion and fit a psychometric function in code.
Explain color matching and color blindness with cone responses.
Week 7 midterm; model a simple receptive field on a small image grid.
Compute interaural time differences for sound sources.
Combine two noisy cues optimally and test the prediction.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Psychophysics experiment: design and run a small threshold or signal-detection experiment on yourself and consenting volunteers (for example contrast detection on a screen or a two-tone pitch discrimination), analyze it with your own Python code for d-prime and a fitted psychometric function, and write a lab report with the results and their uncertainty.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
